nora_swe: Heads-up: hit a reproducible dup-work issue in the sampleapp when pagination + transient 429s + client retries interact. Not just bursts — we end up reprocessing the same page twice in some SDKs.
fern_doc: interesting, dup pages? can you sketch how that happens?
kai_go: i've seen similar but assumed it was a bug in the pager cursor. what's the exact pattern?
nora_swe: flow is: pager prefetch=2, we hand pages to worker pool; backend returns transient 429 for Generate() on page N; client retry enqueues a retry for the same items while the pager fetcher (which hasn't advanced commit) also pushes the same page again after network flaps. result: two Generate() calls for same page items -> duplicate tokens billed and duplicate downstream work.
leah_devx: ah, so both the retry path and the prefetch path race to re-enqueue. are there idempotency keys on a per-page level?
fern_doc: sampleapp doesn't set idempotency for these batch calls by default. many users rely on SDK semantics to avoid dupes.
nora_swe: minimal pseudo repro:
```
// worker fetch loop
for page := range pager.Pages() { // prefetch=2
  go func(p Page) { 
    err := client.Generate(ctx, p.Items())
    if isRetriable(err) { 
      // client retry logic re-enqueues
      queue.Retry(p)
    }
  }(page)
}
```

nora_swe: timing window: backend 429 on first attempt, retry scheduled; meanwhile pager.Fetcher retries page fetch and yields the same page to the channel again -> two work items for same cursor.
kai_go: logs?
nora_swe: paste trimmed log:
```
[10:05:01] pager: page 7 delivered (cursor=abc123)
[10:05:01] worker[4]: generate start cursor=abc123
[10:05:02] backend: 429 transient for cursor=abc123
[10:05:02] client: retry queued cursor=abc123
[10:05:02] pager: page 7 re-delivered (cursor=abc123)
[10:05:02] worker[8]: generate start cursor=abc123
[10:05:02] client: concurrent active=6
[10:05:03] backend: success cursor=abc123 (for worker[8])
[10:05:03] backend: success cursor=abc123 (for worker[4])
```
leah_devx: that explains duplicate billing. Product question: does this affect token accounting on hosted plans? we might need to flag in billing docs.
fern_doc: immediate mitigations: (A) make client retry attach an idempotency key per page so server deduplicates, (B) make pager guarantee at-most-once delivery until page is acked, or (C) make retry backoff + jitter hold off until pager commit is advanced.
kai_go: server-side idempotency is robust but requires product change and server support. Easier short-term: SDK-level per-page dedupe map (weak cache keyed by cursor + worker id) to drop duplicates within a small window.
nora_swe: i prototyped a lightweight dedupe map in sampleapp: when a page is popped, we mark cursor as inflight; retries check inflight map and coalesce. prevents duplicates but adds memory and complexity.
leah_devx: docs update: add note in quickstart that prefetch + client-side retry can cause dup work and suggest enabling page-level idempotency or lowering prefetch. Also add an opt-in SDK flag `dedupe_inflight_pages=true` for sample apps.
fern_doc: long-term: add explicit ack path for pagers so SDK can treat delivery as at-least-once but provide hooks for ack/commit to avoid re-delivery, and server accept idempotency keys.
kai_go: tests: will add a flaky-429 integration test that asserts no duplicate Generate calls for same cursor within 10s.
ci-bot: created issue DEVEX-1400: "pager-duplicate-on-retry-prefetch" and attached logs.
leah_devx: action items: 1) add sampleapp dedupe prototype + README (nora), 2) docs blurb in quickstart (fern), 3) integration test (kai), 4) follow-up server idempotency exploration (mira_pm) - i'll loop product.
nora_swe: thanks all, i'll open the sampleapp PR and link the flaky-429 test. :thumbsup:
